hero: In a teaching corner of a Philippine provincial hospital ward in Pampanga, a Filipino internal medicine resident draws a nephron on a whiteboard while two interns take notes, and in the background an elderly frail Filipino woman rests in a hospital bed with her daughter beside her; warm afternoon light through capiz-style windows, no text.

figures.teaches: Each tubular segment has a main transporter that a drug class blocks, which predicts the drug's effects on sodium, potassium, acid and water.
figures.content: One stylized nephron, glomerulus top left, flowing to the collecting duct at right. Labels with transporter and drug tags: 'Proximal tubule: SGLT2 (SGLT2 inhibitors), carbonic anhydrase (acetazolamide), creatinine secretion (blocked by trimethoprim, cimetidine)'; 'Thick ascending limb: NKCC2 (loop diuretics, furosemide)'; 'Distal convoluted tubule: NCC (thiazides)'; 'Collecting duct principal cell: ENaC (amiloride, trimethoprim), mineralocorticoid receptor (spironolactone, eplerenone, finerenone), V2 receptor / aquaporin-2 (tolvaptan)'. Small arrows: Na+ in, K+ out at collecting duct. Footer: 'Block one segment, the next works harder.' Color code segments in muted teal, amber, green, purple.

figures.teaches: Because serum creatinine is roughly proportional to 1/GFR, losses at high GFR barely change creatinine while losses at low GFR change it sharply.
figures.content: X-axis 'GFR (mL/min/1.73 m2)' 0 to 120; y-axis 'Serum creatinine (mg/dL)' 0 to 8; a hyperbolic curve. Shaded zone on the flat right part labeled 'Flat part: GFR can halve while creatinine stays in the lab range'. Marked points for an example small older woman: 'creatinine 0.5 mg/dL, eGFR about 96' and 'creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, eGFR about 51' with a bracket 'creatinine x2.2, still not flagged'. Steep left part labeled 'Steep part: small GFR changes move creatinine a lot'. Inset note: 'Assumes steady state and stable muscle mass'.
